newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Peters apologises after late-night fracas.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Peters apologises after late-night fracas.

text.p: New Zealand Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters apologised on Thursday for a late-night fracas with a fellow-politician who alleged the flamboyant Maori leader had been drinking.
Peters said he did not have a drinking problem.
Peters, in a radio interview, denied allegations by conservative MP John Banks that he had abused and physically assaulted Banks in a corridor of parliament late on Wednesday.
"I didn't touch the man," he said.

"We were walking down the corridor side by side having a strong conversation. That's not an assault, that's not an abuse, and you'd have to get a forensic scientist to try and find anything that would back that up."
Later, in parliament, Peters acknowledged the two men had had a dispute which had "clearly upset" Banks.
"I wish to tender my apology to him unreservedly," he said.
Banks complained to the speaker of parliament but said he considered the matter closed after Peters's apology.
Interviewed by Television New Zealand, Peters said: "I had a drink. Most members do at that hour of the night. But that had no effect or influence whatsoever," he said.
Asked if he had a drinking problem, he said: "I've got no drinking problem and you personally should not be asking that question of me."
On the same show, left-wing Alliance Party Leader and member of parliament Jim Anderton, who witnessed the incident, said it was clear Peters had been drinking.
"The reason that I take it so seriously is that if Mr Peters, a member of parliament and a senior member of the government can, why can't anyone else," Anderton said.

Peters, flashing his trademark smile, replied: "Mr Anderton is sitting there like some prissy, who is the morals and behaviour cop now in parliament, when he knows full well that there have been events far worse in his own caucus."
Peters steered his New Zealand First party into a coalition with the conservative National Party last December, beoming number two in the government and securing the key Treasurer job.
Banks, a National MP and former cabinet minister, said earlier: "I was assaulted. I was grabbed by the shoulder and close to the scruff of the neck and given one hell of a good shake and push."
He said he thought Peters was going to hit him.

"I really feared for that. Not because I am fearful of being knocked to the ground by him. I don't want to get involved in fighting with people around here, rolling around on the carpets with the deputy prime minister."
Banks alleged Peters had not been in control of himself, and said he should seek help for anger management and drinking.
"I don't know when someone is drunk, but I know when they have drunk too much. He swayed and staggered at me and then I could smell it all over him. And it was very, very strong."
Anderton backed the allegations Peters had manhandled Banks. Anderton and Richard Prebble, leader of the radical free-market Act New Zealand, both complained to parliament's speaker.
